Subject: Private deployment: KMS ownership & data boundaries

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to an internal greenlight to proceed with a private VPC deployment but legal has a few non-negotiables on the DPA and I wanted to confirm Redwood's position before we route the redlines. Key asks from our side: 

- Customer-managed keys (BYOK) with explicit statement that Redwood will not hold keys or be able to decrypt customer data.
- Escrow/escape-hatch procedure: what happens if a customer loses keys, or in an emergency where access is required for remediation?
- Subprocessor visibility and pre-approval for any subprocessors that would touch customer data in the deployment (even for monitoring/alerting).
- Cross-border transfer language: some of our data is EU-based and we need to ensure no transfer without SCCs or equivalent safeguards.

Can you send the latest DPA redline for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and a current subprocessors registry? Also please highlight any clauses where Redwood requires operational access to customer data or keys.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement timeline is tight.

Best,
Sara

Sara —

Thanks for laying this out. Sending our current DPA redline and the subprocessors registry for the private deployment offering (attached). High-level summary below so your legal/procurement team can see the intent before digging into the doc: 

- BYOK: We support customer-managed keys for both VPC and on-prem installations. The standard clause states: "Customer retains sole control of key material; Redwood will not store or have programmatic access to plaintext keys used to encrypt Customer Data."

- Escrow / emergency access: We do not recommend Redwood holding escrow keys. Instead we offer an "emergency access workflow" that requires:
  1) Customer initiation through a signed request + DocuSign approval by an authorized contact,
  2) Two-person Redwood ops approval (manager + security lead),
  3) Access recorded to immutable audit logs and limited to a specified short window.
  This workflow is documented in Section 6 of the attached DPA redline. If FinLedger requires escrow, we can discuss a KMS escrow addendum with a narrow, auditable process — that would be an exception and priced separately.

- Subprocessors: The attached registry lists subprocessors that may be used for monitoring, provisioning, and telemetry in private-mode (e.g., logging aggregation, vulnerability scanning). For private deployments we aim to keep subprocessors minimal; any that have the potential to see customer-controlled data streams require explicit customer acknowledgement. The modern practice is to list categories and provide a 30-day notice for additions.

- Cross-border: Our DPA includes SCCs for EU->US transfers and an option to host private control plane components in EU regions for an additional deployment fee. We can provide a variant that restricts control-plane / logging egress to EU-only with dedicated endpoints.

I attached: DPA_Redline_v1.docx (redline of private-deploy DPA) and subprocessors_registry_20260815.csv.

If legal wants to call this week, I'm happy to join — I can also prepare a short appendix describing the emergency access flow and audit trail sample.

Thanks,
Sergio

Sergio / Priyom —

I reviewed the redline and have a few suggested edits to reduce customer friction while protecting Redwood's operational posture: 

1) Emergency access: Replace any wording that implies Redwood can "decrypt customer data" with a tightly-scoped phrase: "access for data recovery or remediation limited to metadata and application-level artifacts; any decryption requires customer-provided keys or explicit signed authorization as described in Appendix A." This keeps us from taking ownership of plaintext keys.

2) Escrow: If FinLedger insists on escrow, propose an escrow-only addendum with explicit liability limits, audit rights, and a coordinated multi-signature release procedure. Escrow must be opt-in and priced.

3) Subprocessors: Offer a "subprocessor lock" where the customer can require Redwood to notify and obtain consent for any subprocessor added that would have potential to access telemetry or logs. Default remains 30-day notice.

4) Cross-border: Add an option to sign the UK Addendum + SCCs; for customers with strict data locality needs, propose a Dedicated EU Control Plane (separate line item).

I'll prepare a short clean copy incorporating these bullets and a marked-up Appendix A that documents the emergency access steps and log exports. Sergio — happy to join FinLedger's legal call if they want to walk through wording.

-Laura

Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of closing items from our procurement and legal teams: 

- We prefer a no-escrow baseline. The emergency access workflow looks acceptable if the appendix includes the exact audit log fields (who/when/justification) and a sample of the immutable audit export.
- For subprocessors, FinLedger needs a one-time pre-approval for monitoring vendors; ongoing additions can be notified with 30-day notice but require stop-gap mitigation if the vendor will process EU-origin data.
- Cross-border: we'll sign SCCs but would like to include a clause that requires Redwood to notify us within 48 hours of any planned control-plane region change that could affect data residency.

If you can produce a clean DPA incorporating the emergency access appendix and the subprocessor pre-approval language, we can push this through procurement. Please include a DocuSign link when ready.

Sara
